text:
Hi again guys! Looking for advice on if you used a lawyer for the process or not?

At the moment we have a tricky situation: I am a british citizen, but I moved away from the UK as a minor and never went back so I have no drivers license/place of residence/registration there. I have my NIN and passport but thats it. I have been living in Hungary for 6 years but I am not a citizen, I am a permanent resident thanks to Brexit. We both live in Hungary, my wife is a dual citizen here.

Issue is here: I am already married to my wife for over a year, but the UK won't issue me any kind of paperwork reflecting my new status because i simply am not registered at any address or locality there + generally its no longer a certificate they issue for these situations. In Hungary, I am not registered as married because they do not recognise same sex marriages so my status document shows me as single. We have an apostilled marriage certificate from Copenhagen that has already been registered with Israel and Israel has provided my wife with an updated status (sefach/blue paper with ID) of 'married' - not civil partnership, actually married. What do I do here? Where can I get this document and do I actually need it if I am providing the apostilled and translated+notarised marriage certificate?

Some of the documents listed in the document lists are not things we can get due to the weird status we have as both a same sex couple living in a non-accepting country and as a post-brexit british citizen lol. Im wondering if we should consult a lawyer for this after all, and if so, do you guys have any suggestions for lawyers?

Thank you all so much!
